subject: English
passage: Described in treatises mainly published between 1875 and 1965 (such as Charles Henderson and Margaret Foster's Verbatim Court Recording), legal stenography used rapidly written symbols and abbreviations in an attempt to preserve, in print and in real time, the ______ features of witness testimonies—those that result from spontaneous statements of witnesses when adherence to prepared deposition scripts is not required.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's description of witness testimony features. As used in this context, 'unrehearsed' means not practiced or prepared beforehand. The text explains that legal stenography attempted to capture features 'that result from spontaneous statements of witnesses when adherence to prepared deposition scripts is not required.' This emphasis on spontaneity and freedom from prepared scripts indicates that stenographers sought to preserve the improvised, unscripted quality of testimony—in other words, its unrehearsed nature.
